name: Flame / splinter intraretinal hemorrhage
definition: A superficial intraretinal hemorrhage in the retinal nerve fibre layer whose feathered, elongated (flame or splinter) shape follows the radial course of the nerve fibres.

location.notes: Peripapillary and along the arcades where the nerve fibre layer is thickest; splinter hemorrhages may sit on the disc margin; oriented radially toward the disc.

drawing.description: Solid red short feathered strokes oriented along the nerve-fibre direction (radial to the disc); draw one stroke per hemorrhage or a cluster for many.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

name: Dot-blot intraretinal hemorrhage
definition: A round, sharply bordered intraretinal hemorrhage in the deeper (inner nuclear/outer plexiform) retinal layers whose compact shape reflects the vertically oriented tissue in those layers.

location.notes: Posterior pole and midperiphery; in diabetic retinopathy most frequent temporal to the macula; counted per quadrant for severity grading (4-2-1 rule).

drawing.description: Solid red round dots (dot hemorrhages) and slightly larger irregular red blots placed in the quadrant where seen.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

name: Preretinal (subhyaloid / sub-ILM) hemorrhage
definition: Blood trapped between the internal limiting membrane or posterior hyaloid and the retina, typically forming a dense, sharply demarcated boat-shaped pool with a flat upper fluid level that obscures underlying retinal vessels.

location.notes: Premacular or along the arcades/disc in PDR, Valsalva retinopathy, Terson syndrome or ruptured macroaneurysm; blood settles inferiorly giving a horizontal meniscus.

drawing.description: Solid red patch with a straight horizontal superior border (fluid level) and rounded inferior border drawn over the vessels; a sub-ILM bleed may be shown with an inner red ring (double-ring sign). If blood has broken into the vitreous gel, add vitreous blood as green outline filled red.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (P. Dutta Majumder, eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Subretinal / submacular hemorrhage
definition: Blood beneath the neurosensory retina (or beneath the RPE), appearing dark red to grey-green with retinal vessels passing intact over its surface, most often from neovascular AMD, polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy or a ruptured macroaneurysm.

location.notes: Centred on the macula in nAMD/PCV; around the source lesion for macroaneurysm or choroidal rupture; may extend beyond the arcades.

drawing.description: Solid red irregular patch drawn beneath (not over) the retinal vessels, which are drawn crossing it; label 'SRH' or 'sub-RPE' to distinguish depth from intraretinal blood.

name: Roth spot (white-centred hemorrhage)
definition: An intraretinal hemorrhage with a pale white or yellow-white centre (fibrin-platelet plug), a non-specific sign seen in endocarditis, leukaemia, anaemia and other systemic disorders.

location.notes: Posterior pole and peripapillary retina, usually multiple and bilateral.

drawing.description: Red round or flame-shaped hemorrhage drawn as a thick red ring with the central white core left unfilled.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A red = retinal hemorrhage; white centre left uncoloured

name: Microaneurysm
definition: A focal saccular dilation of a retinal capillary wall (from pericyte loss and endothelial proliferation) seen as a tiny, sharply defined red dot; the earliest clinical sign of diabetic retinopathy.

location.notes: Diffuse around the posterior pole, often temporal to the fovea and at the edges of capillary non-perfusion; ring of exudate may surround a leaking cluster.

typical_size: pinpoint, <125 µm (smaller than vein width at disc margin)

drawing.description: Very small solid red dots (smaller than dot hemorrhages) stippled over the involved area.

name: Hard exudates (lipid exudate)
definition: Well-demarcated, waxy yellow deposits of lipid and lipoprotein in the outer plexiform layer from chronic leakage of abnormal retinal vessels, ranging from punctate specks to confluent plaques.

location.notes: Macula and posterior pole, more frequent temporal to the fovea in diabetic retinopathy; often at the edge of thickened retina; plaque-like subfoveal deposits risk subfoveal fibrosis.

drawing.description: Solid yellow dots and irregular yellow plaques at the exact position seen; confluent exudate drawn as a solid yellow patch.

name: Circinate ring of hard exudates
definition: A partial or complete ring of hard exudates surrounding a focal leaking source (microaneurysm cluster, telangiectasia or macroaneurysm), marking the border between oedematous and normal retina.

location.notes: Posterior pole/macula, centred on the leaking lesion; may straddle the fovea.

drawing.description: Ring of yellow dots/plaques encircling the source lesion; draw the central microaneurysms or aneurysm in red inside the ring.

name: Macular star (star figure exudate)
definition: Hard exudates arranged radially in Henle's fibre layer around the fovea, forming a complete or partial star, classically with optic disc oedema in neuroretinitis or with severe hypertensive retinopathy.

location.notes: Centred on the fovea; a partial (nasal) hemi-star is common; may appear 1–2 weeks after disc oedema.

typical_size: 1–2 disc diameters radius around the fovea

drawing.description: Yellow dotted spokes radiating from the fovea (complete or partial star); draw associated disc oedema separately.

name: Cotton-wool spot
definition: A fluffy, white, ill-defined superficial retinal opacity caused by accumulation of axoplasmic debris in the nerve fibre layer after interruption of axoplasmic transport by focal arteriolar occlusion (ischaemia).

location.notes: Within about 3 DD of the disc in the territory of the radial peripapillary capillaries and along the arcades; overlies vessels.

drawing.description: Small fluffy cloud with a soft yellow outline and white centre, drawn over the vessel; keep separate from solid yellow hard exudate dots. (Some charts use green for cotton-wool spots.)

name: Macular edema / retinal thickening
definition: Biomicroscopically visible thickening of the macular retina from intraretinal fluid accumulation, graded by its distance from the foveal centre (centre-involving or not) and often accompanied by hard exudates.

location.notes: Within the arcades; note whether it involves the centre, lies within 500 µm of the centre, or covers ≥1 disc area within 1 DD of the centre.

drawing.description: Outline the thickened area in yellow and hatch it yellow; draw any hard exudates as solid yellow dots at its margin.

name: Cystoid macular edema
definition: Macular oedema in which fluid collects in perifoveal intraretinal cystic spaces arranged radially, giving a honeycomb or petaloid appearance with loss of the foveal reflex.

location.notes: Centred on the fovea; causes include post-cataract surgery (Irvine-Gass), uveitis, diabetes and vein occlusion.

drawing.description: Yellow petaloid rosette of small loculi drawn around the fovea.

name: Neovascularization elsewhere (NVE) – flat
definition: New retinal vessels arising from retinal veins more than 1 disc diameter from the disc that lie flat on the retinal surface, not yet elevated into the vitreous, typically at the border of perfused and non-perfused retina.

location.notes: Along the major arcades and midperiphery adjacent to capillary non-perfusion; size recorded in disc areas (≥1/2 DA is high-risk in PDR).

drawing.description: Fine net or fan of purple lines (or a solid purple patch for dense tufts) arising from the parent vein at the location seen.

name: Neovascularization elsewhere (NVE) – elevated
definition: Retinal new vessels that have grown forward along the posterior hyaloid into the vitreous cavity, often with accompanying fibrous tissue, bleeding into the vitreous when the hyaloid contracts.

location.notes: Arcades/midperiphery at sites of vitreoretinal adhesion; often associated with preretinal or vitreous hemorrhage.

drawing.description: Orange net or frond drawn at the site; add a green outline if fibrous tissue/vitreous attachment is present.

name: Neovascularization of the disc (NVD)
definition: New vessels on the optic disc or within 1 disc diameter of its margin, an ischaemic proliferative sign (diabetes, ischaemic CRVO, ocular ischaemia) whose size is graded against standard photographs.

location.notes: On the disc surface or within 1 DD of the margin; ≥1/4–1/3 disc area defines high-risk PDR.

drawing.description: Fine purple vascular loops/net drawn over the disc circle; switch to orange if the vessels are elevated into the vitreous.

name: Intraretinal microvascular abnormalities (IRMA)
definition: Tortuous, dilated intraretinal vessel segments (shunts or early intraretinal new vessels) adjacent to areas of capillary non-perfusion that do not breach the internal limiting membrane, a marker of severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy.

location.notes: Posterior pole and midperiphery bordering non-perfused retina; graded per quadrant.

drawing.description: Short, irregular, kinked red lines lying within the retina (not raised), drawn between arteriole and venule in the quadrant seen.

name: Venous beading
definition: Localized alternating dilation and constriction of a retinal vein giving a string-of-beads appearance, a sign of severe retinal ischaemia in diabetic retinopathy.

location.notes: Mainly between the first and third venous bifurcations; graded by number of quadrants (≥2 quadrants = severe NPDR by 4-2-1 rule).

drawing.description: Redraw the affected vein segment in blue with a beaded (alternating wide/narrow) contour.

name: Branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO)
definition: Occlusion of a branch retinal vein, usually at an arteriovenous crossing, producing a sectoral, apex-to-crossing wedge of flame and dot-blot hemorrhages, dilated tortuous vein, cotton-wool spots and macular oedema in the drained territory.

location.notes: Wedge with apex at the occluding AV crossing, fanning toward the periphery; superotemporal most common, then inferotemporal; macular branch occlusions are limited to the macula.

drawing.description: Draw the affected vein dilated and tortuous in blue, fill its territory with red flame/blot hemorrhages, mark the occlusion site at the AV crossing in brown, and add yellow for oedema/exudate and cotton-wool spots.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

name: Hemiretinal (hemicentral) vein occlusion
definition: Occlusion of one of the two trunks of a dual-trunked central retinal vein at or near the disc, causing CRVO-type hemorrhages confined to the superior or inferior half of the retina.

location.notes: Respects the horizontal raphe; occlusion site at or behind the disc rather than at an AV crossing.

drawing.description: Red hemorrhages throughout one hemifundus up to the periphery with the corresponding dilated blue vein trunk; mark the occlusion at the disc in brown.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

name: Central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO)
definition: Occlusion of the central retinal vein at or behind the lamina cribrosa producing dilated tortuous veins and hemorrhages in all four quadrants, with disc oedema, cotton-wool spots and macular oedema, classified as non-ischaemic or ischaemic.

location.notes: Hemorrhages extend from disc to periphery; peripheral hemorrhage severity relates to anterior-segment neovascular risk.

drawing.description: All veins drawn dilated and tortuous in blue, red flame/blot hemorrhages in every quadrant, yellow cotton-wool spots/oedema, swollen disc margin, occlusion marked brown at the disc.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

name: Branch retinal artery occlusion (BRAO)
definition: Occlusion of a branch retinal artery, usually embolic at a bifurcation, causing acute opaque whitening (inner retinal infarction) of the retina in the territory supplied distal to the block.

location.notes: Wedge of whitening distal to the occlusion, usually temporal arcade branches; embolus often visible at the proximal bifurcation; whitening resolves over weeks leaving attenuated, sometimes sheathed arterioles.

typical_size: 1–3 clock hours / one sector of the posterior pole

drawing.description: Shade the whitened retinal sector yellow (intraretinal oedema) along the course of the affected red arteriole and mark the occluded segment or embolus in brown.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

name: Central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO)
definition: Occlusion of the central retinal artery producing diffuse whitening of the posterior-pole inner retina with a cherry-red spot at the fovea, attenuated arterioles and sometimes segmented (box-car) blood columns.

location.notes: Whitening most marked in the posterior pole where the ganglion cell layer is thickest; a patent cilioretinal artery spares a tongue of retina between disc and fovea.

typical_size: whole posterior pole within the arcades

drawing.description: Shade the posterior pole yellow (ischaemic oedema), leave a red dot at the fovea (cherry-red spot), draw arteries thin in red with interrupted segments, and mark the occlusion at the disc in brown; leave any cilioretinal-spared tongue unshaded.

name: Cilioretinal artery occlusion
definition: Occlusion of a cilioretinal artery (arising from the posterior ciliary circulation at the disc margin) producing a tongue-shaped zone of retinal whitening between the temporal disc and the fovea, isolated or with CRVO or arteritic disease.

location.notes: Papillomacular bundle region from the temporal disc margin toward the fovea.

drawing.description: Yellow tongue-shaped area of whitening from the temporal disc edge toward the fovea along the cilioretinal vessel (drawn red); mark the vessel origin in brown.

name: Cherry-red spot
definition: Relative red appearance of the foveola, where the retina is thin and the choroid shows through, contrasted against surrounding opaque whitened (ischaemic or storage-laden) perifoveal retina.

location.notes: Exactly at the foveola; seen in acute CRAO, ocular ischaemic syndrome and lysosomal storage diseases.

drawing.description: Solid red dot at the fovea surrounded by a yellow ring/area representing the whitened perifoveal retina.

location.notes: Distributed along the territory of the occluded arteriole (sector, cilioretinal tongue or whole posterior pole).

typical_size: variable; 1/2 DD to whole posterior pole

name: Retinal arterial embolus (Hollenhorst plaque)
definition: Intra-arterial embolic material lodged in a retinal arteriole, classically at a bifurcation: refractile yellow cholesterol (Hollenhorst) plaques, chalky white calcific emboli, or dull grey-white elongated platelet-fibrin emboli.

name: Retinal arterial macroaneurysm (RAM)
definition: An acquired focal fusiform or saccular dilation of a retinal arteriole, usually within its first three bifurcations in elderly hypertensive patients, which may leak (circinate exudate, oedema) or rupture causing multilevel (sub-, intra-, pre-retinal and vitreous) hemorrhage.

location.notes: On a major arcade arteriole, most often the temporal arcades; hemorrhage centred on the aneurysm may hide it.

typical_size: 1/8–1/4 disc diameter aneurysm; hemorrhage up to several DD

name: ROP demarcation line / ridge (stage 1–2)

name: ROP stage 3 extraretinal fibrovascular proliferation
definition: Extraretinal neovascular and fibrous tissue growing from the posterior surface of the ROP ridge into the vitreous (stage 3), graded by extent in clock hours and zone.

location.notes: On the posterior aspect of the ridge; flat, ill-defined neovascular networks may occur posteriorly in aggressive ROP.

drawing.description: Orange band drawn on the posterior side of the ridge over the involved clock hours (purple if flat neovascularization).

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: International Classification of Retinopathy of Prematurity, Third Edition.

name: Purtscher / Purtscher-like retinopathy (Purtscher flecken)
definition: A microembolic occlusive retinopathy after trauma, pancreatitis or other systemic insults, with multiple polygonal yellow-white areas of inner retinal whitening (Purtscher flecken) between arterioles, cotton-wool spots and intraretinal hemorrhages around the disc.

location.notes: Peripapillary and posterior pole, often bilateral; flecken spare a clear zone adjacent to arterioles.

typical_size: flecken 1/4–1 DD each; area several DD

drawing.description: Polygonal yellow patches between the arterioles around the disc, plus cotton-wool spots and red hemorrhages as seen.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A yellow = intraretinal edema (ischaemic whitening)

pubmed.title: [Purtscher disease. Range of variation of clinical manifestations in 11 patients and pathogenetic considerations].
Bilateral Combined Central Retinal Artery and Vein Occlusion in a Child with Purtscher Retinopathy: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.

name: Ocular ischaemic syndrome (midperipheral hemorrhages)
definition: Chronic ocular hypoperfusion from severe carotid obstruction producing narrowed arteries, dilated non-tortuous veins and blot hemorrhages and microaneurysms concentrated in the midperiphery, with possible disc/retinal neovascularization.

location.notes: Hemorrhages in a ring in the midperiphery rather than the posterior pole (distinguishes from diabetic retinopathy/CRVO).

drawing.description: Red blot hemorrhages scattered in a band around the midperiphery; narrow red arteries and dilated blue veins; NVD/NVE in purple/orange.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Ocular ischemic syndrome - a systematic review.
The ocular ischemic syndrome.

name: Hard (small) drusen
definition: Small (<63 µm), discrete, sharply bordered yellow deposits between the RPE and Bruch's membrane; medium drusen measure 63–125 µm and define early AMD.

location.notes: Within 2 DD of the fovea for AMD grading; hard drusen also common in the periphery with ageing.

drawing.description: Fine yellow stipple over the involved area.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (P. Dutta Majumder, eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

pubmed.title: Clinical classification of age-related macular degeneration.
Aging is not a disease: distinguishing age-related macular degeneration from aging.

name: Soft (large) drusen
definition: Large (≥125 µm), pale yellow sub-RPE deposits with indistinct borders that may coalesce (confluent drusen or drusenoid PED), defining intermediate AMD and a high risk of late AMD.

location.notes: Within the macula (2 DD of the fovea), often clustered around the fovea.

typical_size: ≥125 µm each (about the width of a major vein at the disc margin)

drawing.description: Larger yellow round dots with soft edges; merge into a yellow outlined patch when confluent.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (P. Dutta Majumder, eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

pubmed.title: Clinical classification of age-related macular degeneration.

name: Geographic atrophy (GA)
synonyms: complete rpe and outer retinal atrophy
definition: Sharply demarcated, round or lobulated areas of RPE, photoreceptor and choriocapillaris loss through which large choroidal vessels are visible, representing late (atrophic) AMD.

location.notes: Parafoveal first (often foveal-sparing horseshoe), later involving the fovea; multifocal lesions coalesce.

drawing.description: Outline each atrophic area in black and cross-hatch in red (chorioretinal atrophy of attached retina); add brown flecks for marginal pigment.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A paving-stone (chorioretinal atrophy of attached retina) = black outline cross-hatched red

pubmed.title: Clinical classification of age-related macular degeneration.
[Diagnostic approach and treatment paradigm in atrophic age related macular degeneration: Recommendations of the France Macula Federation].

name: Choroidal / macular neovascularization (CNV/MNV)
definition: Neovascular tissue growing from the choroid beneath or through the RPE (type 1, 2) or from the retinal circulation (type 3), seen as a grey-green or yellow-grey subretinal lesion with associated subretinal fluid, hemorrhage, exudate or PED.

location.notes: Subfoveal, juxtafoveal or extrafoveal; also peripapillary, along angioid streaks, lacquer cracks or choroidal ruptures.

drawing.description: Purple patch at the membrane location with surrounding blue for subretinal fluid, red for hemorrhage and yellow for exudate.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A purple = flat neovascularization (CNV lies beneath the retina, not elevated into vitreous)

pubmed.title: Consensus Nomenclature for Reporting Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration Data: Consensus on Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration Nomenclature Study Group.

name: Disciform scar (subretinal fibrosis)
definition: End-stage fibrous (fibroglial) replacement of a macular neovascular lesion, appearing as an elevated white-yellow subretinal plaque with variable pigmentation and overlying retinal atrophy.

location.notes: Subfoveal or centred on the former neovascular lesion.

drawing.description: Yellow (subretinal fibrosis) patch with brown pigment clumps at the margin/within.

color_source: Indirect ophthalmoscopy and fundus drawing (Dr Sonali Raj Singh, SlideShare teaching deck) https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/indirect-ophthalmoscopy-and-fundus-drawing/238698487

pubmed.title: Fibrogliosis in neovascular age-related macular degeneration: A new mechanistic perspective.

name: Pigment epithelial detachment (PED)
definition: Separation of the RPE from Bruch's membrane by fluid, blood, drusenoid material or fibrovascular tissue, seen as a sharply outlined, dome-shaped orange-yellow elevation.

location.notes: Macula (nAMD, PCV, CSC); may be multiple or peripapillary.

drawing.description: Brown round/oval dome with a crisp outline; red notch or fill if hemorrhagic, purple adjacent if vascularized.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (P. Dutta Majumder, eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

pubmed.title: Retinal pigment epithelial detachment: Molecular mechanisms, multimodal imaging classification, and clinical management across the spectrum of macular disease.

name: RPE tear (rip)
definition: A rupture of the RPE at the edge of a PED, with retraction and scrolling of the torn RPE into a hyperpigmented ridge beside a sharply defined crescent of bare Bruch's membrane.

location.notes: At the margin of a vascularized PED, spontaneously or after anti-VEGF; graded by size and foveal involvement.

drawing.description: Crescent outline in brown with the bare area left unfilled and a thick brown line for the scrolled, pigmented RPE edge.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A brown = RPE pigmentation seen through attached retina

pubmed.title: MANAGEMENT OF RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM TEAR DURING ANTI-VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR THERAPY.
ASSOCIATION BETWEEN RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM TEAR AND ANTI-VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR THERAPY: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

name: Central serous chorioretinopathy (serous macular detachment)
definition: A pachychoroid disorder in which choroidal hyperpermeability and RPE dysfunction cause a well-circumscribed, round serous detachment of the neurosensory macula, often with a small PED or yellow subretinal precipitates.

location.notes: Round/oval detachment centred on or near the fovea; chronic cases leave gravitational descending tracts inferiorly.

drawing.description: Blue outlined (and lightly shaded) round area of detached macula; small brown dome for any PED; inferior gravitational tract as a blue/brown band.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Central serous chorioretinopathy: Recent findings and new physiopathology hypothesis.
Pachychoroid disease: review and update.

name: Polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (polyps)
definition: A subtype of type 1 macular neovascularization with aneurysmal polypoidal dilations of a branching vascular network beneath the RPE, seen as orange-red subretinal nodules with serosanguineous PEDs and hemorrhage.

location.notes: Macula or peripapillary region.

typical_size: polyps 1/8–1/2 DD; lesion up to several DD

drawing.description: Orange round nodules at polyp positions, with brown PEDs, red subretinal hemorrhage and blue subretinal fluid as present.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A orange = elevated neovascularization (polyps are elevated aneurysmal neovascular lesions)

pubmed.title: Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy.

name: Vitelliform lesion (adult-onset foveomacular vitelliform)
definition: A round, yellow, slightly elevated subretinal deposit of lipofuscin-laden material between the neurosensory retina and RPE at or near the fovea, often with central pigment.

location.notes: Foveal or perifoveal, usually bilateral and asymmetric.

drawing.description: Solid yellow round dome at the fovea; brown central dot for pigment.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (P. Dutta Majumder, eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

pubmed.title: Multimodal imaging of adult-onset foveomacular vitelliform dystrophy.

name: Epiretinal membrane (ERM)
definition: A fibrocellular preretinal membrane on the inner retinal surface that produces a glistening cellophane reflex and, when it contracts, radiating retinal striae, vessel tortuosity and macular distortion (pucker).

location.notes: Over the macula, often eccentric; striae radiate toward its contraction centre.

drawing.description: Green outline of the membrane with green wavy striae radiating from its centre; draw dragged vessels accordingly.

color_source: Retinal diagram (Dr Sabin Sahu, SlideShare teaching deck) https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044

pubmed.title: Pathophysiology and clinical aspects of epiretinal membrane - review.
Stiffness of retinal and choroidal tissue: a surface wrinkling analysis of epiretinal membranes and choroidal folds.

name: Vitreomacular traction (VMT)
definition: Anomalous posterior vitreous detachment with persistent vitreous attachment to the macula that distorts the fovea (pseudocysts, schisis, elevation), classified as focal (≤1500 µm) or broad (>1500 µm).

location.notes: Perifoveal vitreous separated with residual foveal attachment; confirmed on OCT but taut hyaloid may be seen biomicroscopically.

drawing.description: Green line/outline of the posterior hyaloid converging onto the fovea at the attachment site; yellow for associated foveal cysts.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (P. Dutta Majumder, eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

pubmed.title: The International Vitreomacular Traction Study Group classification of vitreomacular adhesion, traction, and macular hole.

name: Impending macular hole (Gass stage 1)
definition: Loss of the foveal depression with a yellow foveolar spot (stage 1A) or yellow ring (stage 1B) from vitreofoveal traction before a full-thickness defect forms.

location.notes: Exactly at the foveola.

drawing.description: Small yellow dot (1A) or yellow ring (1B) at the fovea.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A yellow = intraretinal edema/deposit (yellow foveal spot)

pubmed.title: [Age-dependent idiopathic macular foramen. Current concepts of the pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment].
New insights into the pathoanatomy of macular holes based on features of optical coherence tomography.

name: Full-thickness macular hole (FTMH)
definition: A round foveal defect interrupting all neural retinal layers from the internal limiting membrane to the RPE, often with a cuff of subretinal fluid, yellow deposits in its base and an overlying operculum.

location.notes: Centred on the foveola; small ≤250 µm, medium 250–400 µm, large >400 µm (OCT minimum width).

drawing.description: Round red hole with blue outline at the fovea (full-thickness break); surrounding cuff of subretinal fluid as a thin blue ring; operculum as a small green oval anterior to it.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: The International Vitreomacular Traction Study Group classification of vitreomacular adhesion, traction, and macular hole.
New insights into the pathoanatomy of macular holes based on features of optical coherence tomography.

name: Lamellar macular hole (LMH)
definition: A partial-thickness foveal defect with irregular foveal contour, a cavity with undermined edges and apparent loss of foveal tissue but an intact outer retina.

location.notes: Foveal; often with lumpy yellow epiretinal proliferation; diagnosis confirmed on OCT.

drawing.description: Small round blue outline at the fovea cross-hatched in red (partial-thickness break).

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Optical coherence tomography-based consensus definition for lamellar macular hole.
Quantitative Analyses of Retinal Traction Force and Metamorphopsia in Lamellar Macular Hole and Related Diseases.

name: Macular pseudohole
definition: A foveal-sparing epiretinal membrane that steepens the foveal pit so that it mimics a hole biomicroscopically, with no loss of foveal tissue.

location.notes: ERM encircles the fovea with a central opening.

drawing.description: Intact red fovea surrounded by a green ring (contracted ERM edge).

color_source: inferred: ERM green per teaching code; intact fovea red per CMS L33567 App A attached retina

pubmed.title: Optical coherence tomography-based consensus definition for lamellar macular hole.

name: Angioid streaks
definition: Irregular, jagged, red-brown to grey linear breaks in a calcified, brittle Bruch's membrane radiating from a peripapillary ring, associated with pseudoxanthoma elasticum, Paget disease and haemoglobinopathies and prone to CNV.

location.notes: Concentric ring around the disc with spokes radiating outward, tapering toward the periphery; may cross the macula.

typical_size: 1–5 disc diameters long, narrower than veins

drawing.description: Brown jagged lines radiating from a brown peripapillary ring; add purple for any associated CNV.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A brown = choroidal/RPE pigmentation seen through attached retina

pubmed.title: Comprehensive review of angioid streaks.
Angioid streaks-related choroidal neovascularization: Clinical features, multimodal imaging-based differential diagnosis, and optimized treatment strategies.

name: Lacquer cracks
definition: Fine, yellowish-white, irregular linear breaks in Bruch's membrane in the posterior pole of pathologically myopic eyes, a 'plus' lesion predisposing to myopic CNV and subretinal hemorrhage.

location.notes: Posterior pole/macula within a staphyloma, often horizontal or branching; acute cracks may show small subretinal hemorrhage.

drawing.description: Thin yellow branching lines at the macula; small red dot for any associated hemorrhage.

color_source: inferred: no published convention; yellow line chosen for yellow-white Bruch's membrane breaks (cf. CMS L33567 App A yellow = chorioretinal lesion), distinct from brown angioid streaks

pubmed.title: International photographic classification and grading system for myopic maculopathy.
Insights on Acute and Chronic Lacquer Cracks as Imaged with Visible Light OCT.

name: Posterior staphyloma
definition: An outpouching of a circumscribed region of the posterior globe with a radius of curvature smaller than the surrounding eye wall, the hallmark of pathologic myopia.

location.notes: Wide macular, narrow macular, peripapillary, nasal or inferior types; its edge is seen as a curvilinear vessel bend/pigmented line.

typical_size: several disc diameters (often whole posterior pole)

drawing.description: Brown curved outline tracing the staphyloma edge around the posterior pole.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (P. Dutta Majumder, eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

pubmed.title: Posterior staphyloma in pathologic myopia.
Understanding Posterior Staphyloma in Pathologic Myopia: Current Overview, New Input, and Perspectives.

name: Myopic chorioretinal atrophy (diffuse / patchy / macular)
definition: Degenerative chorioretinal atrophy of pathologic myopia, from ill-defined yellowish diffuse atrophy to sharply demarcated grey-white patchy atrophy exposing sclera and macular atrophy, graded in META-PM categories 2–4.

location.notes: Peripapillary and macular, within the staphyloma.

drawing.description: Black outline cross-hatched red for patchy/macular atrophy (dashed outline for diffuse atrophy); brown for marginal pigment.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A paving-stone (chorioretinal atrophy of attached retina) = black outline cross-hatched red

pubmed.title: International photographic classification and grading system for myopic maculopathy.

name: Fuchs spot
definition: A round, dark pigmented macular lesion representing RPE hyperplasia over a regressed myopic choroidal neovascular membrane, a 'plus' lesion of pathologic myopia.

location.notes: Foveal or juxtafoveal in highly myopic eyes.

drawing.description: Solid brown round spot at the macula.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: International photographic classification and grading system for myopic maculopathy.

name: Bull's-eye maculopathy
definition: A ring of parafoveal RPE depigmentation sparing the central fovea, giving a target appearance, classically in advanced hydroxychloroquine/chloroquine toxicity and some cone dystrophies.

location.notes: Annulus around the fovea (pericentral pattern in Asian patients may lie near the arcades).

drawing.description: Brown annulus around a spared red foveal centre.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A brown = RPE pigment change seen through attached retina

pubmed.title: Mimickers of hydroxychloroquine retinal toxicity.
Target in Sight: A Comprehensive Review of Hydroxychloroquine-Induced Bull's Eye Maculopathy.

name: Choroidal (chorioretinal) folds
definition: Alternating light and dark parallel undulations of the inner choroid, Bruch's membrane and RPE across the posterior pole, caused by hypotony, orbital mass, scleritis, hyperopia or idiopathically.

location.notes: Usually horizontal or oblique lines across the macula, sometimes concentric around the disc.

drawing.description: Brown parallel lines across the involved posterior pole following the fold orientation.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A brown = choroidal/RPE change seen through attached retina

pubmed.title: [Choroidal folds].
Stiffness of retinal and choroidal tissue: a surface wrinkling analysis of epiretinal membranes and choroidal folds.

name: Traumatic choroidal rupture
definition: A traumatic break in the choroid, Bruch's membrane and RPE, typically an arc-shaped yellow-white streak concentric to the disc in the posterior pole, often initially hidden by subretinal hemorrhage and later complicated by CNV.

location.notes: Crescentic, concentric to the optic disc, frequently submacular.

drawing.description: Yellow crescent concentric to the disc with brown pigmented margins; red subretinal blood if acute; purple if CNV develops.

color_source: inferred: no published convention; yellow for exposed sclera/atrophy with brown RPE pigment margins (CMS L33567 App A brown)

pubmed.title: Post-Traumatic Choroidal Rupture: Characteristics, Management and Outcomes.

name: Commotio retinae (Berlin oedema)
definition: Transient grey-white opacification of the outer retina after blunt trauma due to photoreceptor outer-segment disruption, at the macula (Berlin oedema) or periphery at the site of impact or contrecoup.

location.notes: Posterior pole (Berlin) or peripheral at the impact site; may be accompanied by choroidal rupture or hemorrhage.

drawing.description: Yellow stippled area of whitening; a red foveal dot if a pseudo-cherry-red spot is present.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Severe Macular Commotio Retinae Following a Fall from a Horse in a Pediatric Patient.
Commotio Retinae.

name: Elschnig spots / Siegrist streaks (hypertensive choroidopathy)
definition: Signs of choroidal ischaemia in malignant hypertension: Elschnig spots are multifocal yellowish RPE lesions over infarcted choriocapillaris lobules that later become pigmented with a pale halo, and Siegrist streaks are linear hyperpigmented lines along sclerosed choroidal arteries.

location.notes: Posterior pole and midperiphery; often with serous retinal detachment and hypertensive retinopathy signs.

drawing.description: Acute: yellow spots; healed: brown dots with a pale yellow halo; Siegrist streaks as short brown lines along choroidal vessel courses; any serous detachment in blue.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A yellow = chorioretinal lesion (acute) and brown = RPE/choroidal pigmentation (healed)

pubmed.title: Ischemic Choroidal Diseases.
Hypertensive choroidopathy in atypical hemolytic-uremic syndrome.
